rules.requiredOutcome: Every retained schema migrates atomically to the current editable schema without mutating its input.
rules.currentBehavior: Schemas 1 through 8 are validated and migrated to schema 9; a failed migration publishes no partial project.

rules.requiredOutcome: The current raw project schema validates, clones, and routes as editable at the core load and migration boundary.
rules.currentBehavior: Schema 9 is the maintained writable raw-project schema and is cloned at the load boundary; this rule does not claim feature-requirement handling at the portable-archive or controller boundary.

rules.requiredOutcome: A bounded pathless main-owned service validates the maintained exact-current-schema project domain before host staging and catalog publication and before returning a shared read document; the renderer repeats validation as defense in depth, without receiving filesystem paths, catalog entry IDs, or lease capabilities. Main-owned startup reclamation preserves every current or recoverable catalog reference, retires abandoned registered stage attempts without removing live writer state, and makes fair progress across a shared bounded budget.
rules.currentBehavior: A fresh filesystem library scope v2 ignores rather than migrates the prior shared v1 scope; a schema 1 database found at the v2 path is rejected instead of implicitly migrated. Metadata schema 2 binds a separate opaque library entry ID to the bounded project identity, exact schema 9, project revision, byte length, SHA-256 digest, and derived immutable revision-and-digest path. The main-only store canonicalizes the document with the bounded tagged-binary Scape codec, enforces the non-raiseable 256 MiB document ceiling, validates root schema, identity, title, and revision, and reserves its canonical path plus one unique random attempt in lease- and fencing-token-bound authoritative project and stage inventories in the same immediate transaction before exclusive stage creation. When exact-lease cleanup is acknowledged, an exclusive-open failure retires only the registration without unlinking the path, while an error after exclusive creation targets that registered random stage for removal. Lost-lease or failed cleanup leaves the registration for takeover. Successful materialization requires the exact metadata and stage paths, lease ID, and fencing token, then atomically renames and syncs the file, marks the canonical row materialized, removes the stage row, verifies the immutable file against the catalog descriptor, and requires every catalog reference to have a materialized row before publishing an exact +1 catalog revision through the fenced metadata journal. The main-owned identity service applies the shared strict exact-V9 maintained-persistence-domain validator before permitting host staging or catalog publication of a renderer commit; it validates the loaded commit result and a stored project again before returning either canonical document. Every serialized project receives a raw-JSON structural preflight capped at 101,536 JSON values and depth 130 before JSON.parse; each exact-V9 decoded codec traversal and maintained-domain validation phase is independently capped at 100,000 nodes and depth 128. The service threads these lower-only caps through renderer input, loaded commit results, stored reads, and response serialization. Renderer input refusal precedes host mutation or staging; an over-budget loaded commit result is refused before the renderer response, although host publication may already have completed. Future-schema tag-shaped data is structurally counted but is neither decoded nor interpreted. Canonical JSON-derived graphs and ordinary direct objects reject accessors, toJSON hooks, method-shadowed arrays, hidden or symbol data, cycles, exotic containers, and non-JSON scalars without invoking application accessors; hostile proxies and prototype-polluted or exotic injected graphs remain outside that code-safety claim. Counters reset between the lexical, codec, validator, and serialization phases, so these per-phase shape ceilings are not an aggregate work, CPU or elapsed-time, allocation-amplification, cancellation, or resident-memory budget. The validator strictly checks core project, document, media, and graph structures without loading legacy migrations or executable effect and worker runtimes. All audio effects must be cloneable and have the generic effect identity, enabled, and parameter structure; type-specific semantic checks currently cover missing-effect compatibility metadata and parametric EQ, while other first- and third-party effect payload semantics are intentionally not gated yet. The host serializes commits and renews its lease while draining admitted work. After journal recovery and before host exposure, main-only startup maintenance walks the authoritative project and stage inventories by monotonic row IDs, captures independent cycle high-waters, persists both cursors plus an alternating schedule, and scans at most 100,000 total rows per invocation in at-most-64-row batches under immediate SQLite writer fences with exact lease checks before and after filesystem work. A current exact-lease stage remains live; a stale registered regular stage is removed; a missing attempt retires; and a non-regular target or non-direct parent remains untouched and inventoried. Canonical rows owned by the current lease or referenced by an outstanding stage remain ineligible. Stage-cycle completion persists and consumes a canonical rescan flag atomically so retired attempts cannot leave already-scanned parents behind. Canonical batches rebuild portable case-folded reachability from the current catalog plus both sides of any pending recovery journal before moving an unreachable registered canonical regular immutable file through a deterministic noncatalogable quarantine. Unregistered stage-looking, canonical, forged quarantine, and foreign files do not consume inventory budget and remain untouched. A real 100,001-row fixture proves successive bounded passes reach the suffix; later inserts wait for the next high-water cycle; and low- and mixed-cap stage fixtures prove persisted alternation and canonical rescanning. The collector yields between batches, safely retries crash-left quarantine files, fails closed on a static symlinked project root or corrupt metadata, and leaves malformed names, non-regular or symlink entries, and managed-media content untouched. Its identity service and owner-scoped IPC expose only bounded project summaries, canonical documents, identities, and delete results; main strips catalog internals, while renderer-owner revocation fences new work and drains admitted operations. The renderer repository repeats the same maintained-persistence-domain exact-V9 validation as defense in depth before local mutation, keeps revision and source/media data in a product-local shadow, treats the shared latest document and summary list as authoritative, and fails closed on an incomplete desktop bridge. A composed source-free editor fixture creates and autosaves in Soundscaper, closes the fenced host, discovers and bootstrap-reopens the same identity and revision from a fresh Framescaper-local store, and commits the next revision in Framescaper while the shared media catalog remains empty. A maintained dedicated Linux x64 CI job builds two separate unpacked packages and runs sequential Soundscaper to Framescaper to Soundscaper processes. They share only one isolated appData root, use separate product profiles, and the final process reuses the Soundscaper profile. Each process waits until the renderer is ready, drives the bounded pathless preload IPC, exact-SHA-256 verifies the expected canonical source-free schema 9 document, commits revisions 1, 2, and 3, checks the renderer summary and main-only catalog row, requires clean recovery, no stale takeover, strictly higher fencing tokens, increasing catalog revisions, and the expected preferred product, and awaits process exit and lease release before continuing. Combined with the composed editor fixture, this closes only the generic packaged source-free preload/IPC/multi-process/executable lifecycle gap. It does not qualify packaged controller autosave or tab activation; source-bearing bytes, playback, or managed media; concurrent opens; crash or stale takeover; interruption or power loss; parent-, database-, or project-root path identity; installers or file associations; or Windows, macOS, or ARM64. Activation-specific feature-capability evaluation and rendered-fallback byte verification remain editor-owned. Third-party activation gating is deliberately outside this slice. Legacy Soundscaper library migration is also deliberately outside this slice. Unregistered or legacy pre-inventory stage-looking files remain foreign and are not adopted or deleted. Migration from the prior shared v1 scope or product-private Soundscaper libraries is intentionally not a current priority and remains deferred and unsupported by this current-only contract; Audacity project import compatibility is a separate boundary.

rules.requiredOutcome: An authoritative latest exact-schema-9 desktop shared-project load with reachable source references must either complete bounded sequential recipient-local readability admission before local shadow mutation and activation or fail closed without replacing the recipient's latest local shadow or adding the remote revision to recipient-local history.
rules.currentBehavior: The renderer collects at most 4,094 reachable timeline, Project Bin, and fallback source references. The pre-existing latest recipient-local exact-schema-9 snapshot of the same project must bind each logical source identity, kind, storage key, MIME type, frame and sample geometry, and kind-specific media descriptor; names and opaque extensions are not provenance. Compatible same-kind descriptors sharing one physical storage key are verified once, while conflicting bindings reject. Payload geometry is capped at 65,536 PCM chunks, while one cumulative 64 GiB budget charges canonical audio archive bytes, including four framing bytes per chunk, and recipient-local video metadata sizes together. A successful body qualification reads selected source or media metadata before and after that body, fully consumes ordered Float32Array PCM with exact chunk, channel, and frame geometry and matching supplied index or frame fields, and reads and SHA-256 hashes each genuine Blob through bounded 4 MiB windows with legacy PCM-on-read migration and media-digest backfill disabled. A pre-existing retained-video digest must match when present; audio and digestless retained video are availability- and geometry- or size-qualified but are not authenticated against a prior content digest. Every failure raised by this repository admission, including mismatch of that video digest, occurs before local shadow save or activation. The later controller-owned rendered-fallback-declaration digest check instead follows repository shadowing but precedes activation side effects. Source-free latest loads perform no source or media I/O. The bootstrap lifetime signal reaches latest load and preserves the exact cancellation reason while admission reads are active, although injected non-cooperative provider work may continue after rejection and a cancellation racing the non-abortable shadow save is not abort-atomic. One repository instance serializes latest load, save, and delete per project. Publication and retention resolve logical references to durable storage keys. Real-store mixed audio and video fixtures qualify bytes already present and bound by the latest local snapshot; composed cross-product evidence covers source-free success and a source-bearing Soundscaper-to-Framescaper fixture whose matching pre-existing descriptor but missing PCM leaves the pre-existing revision unchanged and does not activate. This is a bounded sequential admission-time readability check, not an atomic snapshot, content transfer, publisher authentication, or a durable byte lease. Selected metadata is reread around each body, but body reads are not transactionally bound to it; same-metadata replacement during the sequential observations can go undetected, and replacement or deletion afterward is not fenced. It does not serialize separate repository instances or processes or validate source-bearing saves or explicit local revision loads. A fresh recipient lacks both the prerequisite local descriptor snapshot and automatic acquisition; copy, relink, managed storage, codec playback, and packaged handoff remain unqualified. Existing V1-V8 raw-project migrations remain maintained. Compatibility beyond those retained raw-document migration paths, especially migration from the prior shared v1 scope or product-private Soundscaper libraries, remains unsupported and is not a current priority; Audacity project import is separate. Other first- and third-party effect semantics remain intentionally not gated.

rules.requiredOutcome: Current raw project documents carry a bounded normalized declarative feature-requirements manifest, retained-schema migrations do not invent publisher declarations, maintained exact-current-schema create, load, clone, and commit paths reconcile editor-owned first-party declarations from project state, and pure evaluation classifies caller-declared availability without activating project data.
rules.currentBehavior: Schema 9 validates and deep-clones manifest schema 1, canonical feature identifiers, unique requirement IDs, closed dispositions, bounded collections and strings, and rendered-fallback descriptor source kind and digest syntax. Exact-schema-9 create, load, clone, and commit reconcile the reserved soundscaper.audio-effects bypass requirement when a maintained first-party processor exists in a non-label or non-video track, mixer group, mixer send, or master rack, and the reserved soundscaper.video-effects bypass requirement when a maintained first-party video effect exists on a timeline or Project Bin video clip. Disabled effects and inactive audio racks still declare preservation; missing or foreign effect types and video-effect stacks on non-video clips do not. An explicit publisher declaration for the same capability wins without duplication, and conflicting use of either reserved requirement ID rejects. V1-V8 migration starts from an empty publisher manifest and applies the same owned reconciliation. Evaluation reports available, unavailable, and unknown requirements while retaining the declared bypass or rendered-fallback disposition separately from the native, bypassed, or rendered-fallback effective disposition without mutating the manifest.

rules.requiredOutcome: A current-schema portable archive retains the normalized feature-requirements manifest and every fallback-only source asset, including consistent known source-reference rewriting on copy collisions.
rules.currentBehavior: Schema 9 rendered-fallback descriptors root source metadata during project and history compaction. Current-format .scape export serializes the manifest and every project source asset, import preserves the manifest and its evaluation semantics, and copy import rewrites known fallback source IDs through the same collision map as source identity. Digest integrity is governed by the route-specific current-scape-rendered-fallback-integrity rule; arbitrary future schemas remain outside this rule.

rules.requiredOutcome: Current-format, exact-current-schema .scape routes bind every rendered fallback claim to its canonical archive asset and reject a kind or digest mismatch before publication.
rules.currentBehavior: Export snapshots the admitted project root and complete source records before asynchronous asset work and serializes the same source snapshots and bounded normalized fallback manifest used for validation. Project-root and source-record accessors and callable toJSON hooks are rejected without invocation so they cannot rewrite the admitted serialization; export then hashes every emitted source body and rejects a mismatch against the completed descriptors before manifest write or destination commit. Import and inspection bind each exact-schema-9 fallback source ID, kind, and SHA-256 to the canonical manifest asset before collision lookup or storage; import then verifies the extracted asset body size and SHA-256 before source or project publication. Inspection performs descriptor binding only and does not read or hash asset bodies. Copy import rewrites the source ID while preserving the verified digest. Future schemas return and featureRequirements is not traversed. Raw-project and stored-project loads plus runtime fallback use remain outside this route-specific integrity rule.

rules.requiredOutcome: Maintained current-schema projects are evaluated against a stable selected-product capability registry before activation, and every unavailable or unregistered requirement makes the document intrinsically read-only with a per-tab compatibility report.
rules.currentBehavior: Explicit stable broad org.soundscaper.capability feature IDs map one-to-one to the capability keys in both maintained product profiles. Only a strict true profile value is available; registered non-true capabilities are unavailable and unregistered feature IDs are unknown. The controller evaluates exact schema 9 from the actual project history that will be activated before activation side effects and makes every report containing an unavailable or unknown requirement intrinsically read-only. When an existing same-ID tab wins, its stored read-only declaration also wins over the ignored incoming document's flags. The report is retained per tab, remains deeply frozen across session metadata clones, and is exposed on the document snapshot. Future schemas return no report and featureRequirements is not traversed. A separate controller-admission rule verifies declared fallback bytes; runtime fallback use remains outside this report rule.

rules.requiredOutcome: An activated exact-current-schema document with an incompatible feature report keeps a persistent structured notice associated with the active tab without activating project data or offering a compatibility override.
rules.currentBehavior: The maintained workspace consumes the active document snapshot's deeply frozen featureRequirementsCompatibility report directly. When compatible is false, it derives a separate frozen notice from only unavailable and unknown items, recomputes their counts, and persistently displays a non-dismissible localized document-level region with bounded display names, stable feature IDs, availability, and the declared bypass or rendered-fallback disposition whenever that project tab is active. The effective disposition remains available as structured metadata rather than being mislabeled as the declaration. Available items are excluded; evaluator messages and fallback internals are not read or rendered; and the notice exposes no activation controls or generic rendered-fallback substitution or third-party-loading claim; the exact first-party audio active-playback indicator is bound by its separate rule. Switching to a compatible or null-report tab removes the notice, and switching back restores it from that active tab's report. Future schemas produce a null report, and the workspace does not inspect their featureRequirements value. Outside the separate first-party audio- and video-effect rules, this document-level notice is not a generic affected-object placeholder, per-feature bypass control, runtime fallback selection, future-schema guarantee, or third-party activation gate.

rules.requiredOutcome: On maintained exact-current-schema activation, unavailable maintained first-party audio rack effects declared for bypass reach the editor engine only through a bounded non-persisted bypass projection while canonical state remains unchanged and every affected object stays visibly identified on its active tab.
rules.currentBehavior: The controller evaluates the authoritative actual project history and projects only exact schema 9 when its soundscaper-project report contains a registered audioEffects item that is unavailable, declares bypass, and has the effective bypassed disposition. Active, enabled, not-already-bypassed maintained processors in non-label and non-video track, mixer-group, mixer-send, and master racks become minimal bypassed engine copies; inactive racks, disabled or already-bypassed effects, and missing or foreign effect types remain untouched. Stable IDs and effect types are bounded, the lower-only production ceiling is 4,096 affected effects, overflow rejects instead of truncating, and placeholder metadata never reads or retains effect params, context, state, or other payloads. Only engine loading receives the projection: the canonical project, history, source loading, persistence, and save paths remain unchanged. Projection metadata is deeply frozen across per-tab session clones and the document snapshot. The active compatibility notice matches that metadata to one qualifying requirement and renders localized control-free affected-effect placeholders with maintained effect labels and canonical track, group, send, or master ownership without reading effect payloads. Future schemas return unchanged before rack traversal. This rule does not cover unknown or third-party effects, rendered-fallback substitution, offline render or export, per-feature activation controls, or arbitrary future schemas.

rules.requiredOutcome: On maintained exact-current-schema activation, one unavailable registered first-party audioEffects requirement declared for rendered fallback replaces canonical audio paths with its admitted mono or stereo whole-mix only for editor playback while canonical state remains unchanged and activation stays visibly identified.
rules.currentBehavior: The controller evaluates the authoritative actual project history and projects only exact schema 9 when its soundscaper-project report contains exactly one registered audioEffects item that is unavailable with declared and effective rendered-fallback dispositions, and the report descriptor exactly matches the canonical manifest requirement. One referenced audio source must be mono or stereo, use its full safe frame range from frame zero, and match the project sample rate and master channel count; ADM and surround projects reject, as do ambiguous candidates, missing or mismatched sources, and unsafe geometry, while reserved synthetic track or clip ID collisions also reject. The transient projection removes canonical audio clips and tracks, installs one neutral whole-mix clip and track, neutralizes mixer and master processing, and retains video and label timing. The shared playback project service applies the same projection during initial activation and later engine reapplies. Required stored metadata is rechecked; short sources are decoded and their buffer geometry must match exactly, while oversized sources must expose a streamable chunk provider. Readiness does not prefetch or revalidate streamed chunks, so later provider failure remains possible. Initial activation prepares only the required fallback source before acquiring the session activation reservation or performing activation side effects. Metadata, audio-context, and decoded-body operations race the controller-lifetime signal, reject cancellation promptly with its exact reason, and fence late settlement from publishing buffers, chunk providers, engine chunk sources, missing-source state, or status. A readiness failure leaves the active project, tab, and lock unchanged. Ordinary-source transient buffers are later merged with prepared fallback buffers before projected engine load. The canonical project, history, persistence, save, export, and offline render paths remain unchanged. Deeply frozen per-tab and document-snapshot metadata drives one persistent localized active during editor playback indicator without exposing the source ID or digest. Controller digest admission is point-in-time and is not a durable byte lease. Successful prepared cache or stream-provider state is reusable and is not rolled back if reservation or later activation fails. Canonical playback reapply through ensureProjectSourcesAvailable remains identity-fenced but non-abortable. Generic or video fallback, ADM or surround playback, freeze and proxy authoring, unknown or third-party activation, future schemas, and earlier Soundscaper schemas remain outside this rule.

rules.requiredOutcome: On maintained exact-current-schema activation, unavailable maintained first-party video effects declared for bypass reach editor playback only through a bounded non-persisted bypass projection while canonical state remains unchanged and every affected timeline or Project Bin effect stays visibly identified on its active tab.
rules.currentBehavior: The controller evaluates the authoritative actual project history and projects only exact schema 9 when its soundscaper-project report contains a registered videoEffects item that is unavailable, declares bypass, and has the effective bypassed disposition. Enabled maintained effects on timeline and Project Bin video clips become minimal disabled activation copies; disabled effects and missing, foreign, or wrong-kind stacks remain untouched. Stable clip and effect IDs are bounded to 256 characters, effect types to 128 characters, the lower-only production ceiling is 4,096 affected effects across both locations, and overflow rejects instead of truncating. Each placeholder entry records only location, clip ID, effect ID, and effect type without reading or retaining params, context, state, or other opaque payloads. Only transient engine loading receives the project projection, and the WebGL preview filters exact affected effects from timeline stacks using trusted metadata while caching selectors and preserving unchanged stack references. The canonical project, history, source loading, persistence, save, and export or offline-render paths remain unchanged. Projection metadata is deeply frozen across per-tab session clones and the document snapshot. The active compatibility notice matches that metadata to one qualifying requirement and renders localized control-free affected-effect placeholders with maintained effect labels and canonical Timeline or Project Bin clip ownership without reading effect payloads. Future schemas return unchanged before clip or Project Bin traversal. This rule does not cover unknown or third-party effects, rendered-fallback substitution, export or offline render behavior, per-feature activation controls, arbitrary future schemas, or earlier Soundscaper project schemas.

rules.requiredOutcome: Every rendered fallback referenced by an exact-current-schema raw or stored project admitted through the maintained controller is verified against its canonical local stored bytes before activation side effects.
rules.currentBehavior: The controller verifies the authoritative exact-schema-9 activation project, including existing same-ID tab history bound by a session-owned history token. After verification it obtains one exclusive session activation reservation before project-generation invalidation, recording or engine shutdown, lock changes, ordinary engine-source loading, or normal activation persistence. The reservation rejects target history replacement, close/reopen, and competing active-project publication through synchronous session publication and is released in finally. Admission reads disable on-access PCM migration scheduling and retained-media digest claim/backfill, so verification does not publish storage maintenance. Audio claims hash the canonical audio-f32le-chunks-v1 sequence through the same checked PCM geometry and cumulative 65,536-chunk ceiling as .scape export. Video claims hash a genuine immutable original-media Blob body incrementally through the non-raiseable 4 MiB media-digest window. Unique claimed audio bytes and admitted video sizes share a non-raiseable 64 GiB cumulative ceiling before fallback body reads. Verification is sequential and cooperatively cancellable through the maintained store. Read-only video-metadata preflight is raced against cancellation, so an injected signal-ignoring provider may continue after admission rejects; a provider-stalled fallback body read can instead delay cancellation settlement and iterator cleanup. Verification deduplicates identical source claims, rejects conflicting digests before storage reads, and rejects missing, malformed, or mismatched local assets. Empty manifests and future schemas perform no asset reads, and future featureRequirements are not traversed. This admission-time rule does not verify arbitrary direct store.loadProject calls, continuously bind against later low-level source replacement, establish publisher authenticity, substitute fallback media at runtime, or provide a complete third-party activation gate.

rules.requiredOutcome: Current-format portable archive inspection evaluates maintained project feature requirements against the selected product before collision lookup, import, persistence, or activation without interpreting future project schemas.
rules.currentBehavior: The selected product is snapshotted through the shared compatibility service and injected into inspection as a provider-owned option after caller options, so a caller cannot override it. After current-format archive integrity, project-source validation, and rendered-fallback claim-to-descriptor binding, exact schema 9 is evaluated before project collision lookup and returned as a deeply frozen featureRequirementsCompatibility report. Inspection does not hash asset bodies. Future project schemas return null and featureRequirements is not traversed. This programmatic surface is the foundation for the maintained open decision; it does not use fallbacks at runtime or gate third-party activation.

rules.requiredOutcome: Every current-format, exact-current-schema archive opened through the maintained workspace/UI file routes with an incompatible selected-product feature report requires explicit compatibility-bearing consent or cancellation before import, persistence, or activation, in both collision and no-collision flows.
rules.currentBehavior: Maintained workspace/UI file-open routes use one replaceable owned request from inspection through a closed decision. A no-collision incompatible report permits only open-read-only or cancel; a combined incompatibility and ID collision permits only copy-read-only or cancel in one decision; compatible collisions permit only copy or cancel. Distinct compatibility-bearing choices fail closed against stale collision callbacks. Cancel resolves before native import, persistence, or activation. The localized dialog exposes bounded display names, stable feature IDs, availability, and declared disposition without claiming fallback verification or runtime use; incompatible decisions default focus to Cancel and support Escape dismissal and focus restoration. Acceptance passes only the existing copy collision policy into native open, after which the controller reevaluates the actual project history and enforces it as intrinsically read-only. Future-schema null reports skip this decision. The low-level native-open API retains its caller-supplied collision policy, and it and third-party activation remain outside this rule.

rules.requiredOutcome: A raw project document with a newer schema is cloned without normalization and cannot enter a mutation or overwrite path.
rules.currentBehavior: The core migration boundary returns newer objects as structured clones with readOnly=true and reason=newer-schema.

rules.requiredOutcome: A future-schema portable archive opens read-only and can be exported unchanged without ID, storage-key, binary, or unknown-field loss.
rules.currentBehavior: The archive importer traverses known collections and may rewrite project and source identity, so arbitrary future-schema .scape round trips are not yet claimed.

rules.requiredOutcome: Designated JSON opaque extension fields survive migration, clone, save, and portable archive reopen semantically unchanged.
rules.currentBehavior: Legacy unknown JSON fields are collected under opaqueExtensions.legacyV1 and JSON-compatible opaqueExtensions survive current-schema .scape round trips.

rules.requiredOutcome: Supported Uint8Array and ArrayBuffer opaque state in exact-current-schema, current-format .scape projects uses a tagged, bounded JSON encoding and round-trips byte-exactly without activation.
rules.currentBehavior: Before JSON.parse, every schema receives an iterative raw-JSON structural preflight bounded to 101,536 values and depth 130 in production; the descriptor allowance preserves round-trip closure for the bounded tagged representation. Exact schema 9 export encodes Uint8Array values, offset-view bytes, and ArrayBuffer values with a reserved tagged descriptor; export and post-parse decode independently enforce the lower-only logical limits of 100,000 traversal nodes and depth 128, while other ArrayBuffer views reject. The binary budget also admits at most 256 payloads, 4 MiB per payload, and 8 MiB aggregate bytes. Import and inspection validate the closed descriptor schema, unique positive IDs, canonical base64, exact byte lengths, and all limits before allocating decoded payloads, then restore the declared binary type without interpreting its bytes. Reserved-tag collisions, project-container accessors, and callable container toJSON hooks reject without invocation. Future-schema tag-shaped data is structurally counted by the raw preflight but is neither decoded nor interpreted as a binary descriptor.

rules.requiredOutcome: Unavailable native features remain visible and bypassable, retain editable opaque state, declare requirements, and reference an audible or visible fallback when available.
rules.currentBehavior: The schema 9 manifest, evaluator, retention roots, current-format .scape paths, selected-product controller report, and current-format .scape inspection report preserve and classify declared requirements. Maintained exact-schema-9 create, load, clone, and commit paths reconcile the owned first-party audio- and video-effects requirements. The bounded first-party audio-effect slice loads qualifying unavailable rack processors through a transient engine bypass projection, and the bounded first-party video-effect slice loads minimal disabled activation copies and filters exact affected effects from timeline stacks in WebGL preview; persistent localized control-free affected-object placeholders follow the active tab for both slices. A separate exact-schema-9 first-party audio whole-mix rendered-fallback slice substitutes one admitted mono or stereo source only for editor playback while canonical state remains unchanged and the active tab identifies that fallback use. Maintained opens provide an actionable pre-open read-only or cancel decision, the broader persistent document-level post-open report follows the active tab, and the controller still makes an activated project with an unavailable or unknown requirement intrinsically read-only. Current-format exact-schema .scape archive fallback integrity verifies the declared digest against the canonical asset, while inspection performs pre-collision descriptor binding without reading asset bodies. Maintained exact-schema-9 controller activation also verifies referenced local audio and video fallback bytes before activation side effects. The bounded current-schema .scape codec preserves supported Uint8Array and ArrayBuffer opaque native/effect state byte-exactly without activation; other buffer views remain unsupported. Generic per-object placeholders and per-feature bypass controls beyond these maintained first-party audio- and video-effect slices, rendered-fallback runtime use beyond the first-party audio whole-mix playback slice, and arbitrary future-schema archive preservation are not implemented.

rules.requiredOutcome: Video originals and reproducible proxies retain an explicit relationship, and proxy use never changes editorial time or original delivery semantics.
rules.currentBehavior: Video source originals are retained, but the roadmap proxy relationship and offline/relink model are not implemented.

rules.requiredOutcome: Freeze, unfreeze, commit, and rendered fallback state preserve the editable source and native-effect metadata.
rules.currentBehavior: Offline rendering and the narrow exact-schema-9 playback fallback exist, but no canonical authored freeze, unfreeze, commit, relink, or rendered-fallback document state and no generic cross-platform fallback-authoring contract are implemented.

rules.requiredOutcome: An unknown .scape container format is rejected before project or media persistence rather than guessed or partially imported.
rules.currentBehavior: The manifest parser accepts only formatVersion 1 and import staging rolls back source writes on failure.
